props.name: value
props.description:
The value of the currently active `Tab`. Use when the component is controlled.
When the value is `null`, no Tab will be active.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description:
The default value. Use when the component is not controlled.
When the value is `null`, no Tab will be active.

props.name: orientation
props.description: The component orientation (layout flow direction).

props.name: onValueChange
props.description:
Callback invoked when new value is being set.

The event `reason` is `'none'` for user-initiated changes, such as a click
or keyboard navigation; `'initial'` for the first automatic selection or
fallback in uncontrolled roots when `defaultValue` is omitted or
`undefined`, including when the implicit initial value is disabled or
missing; `'disabled'` for automatic fallback when the selected tab becomes
disabled in uncontrolled roots; or `'missing'` for automatic fallback when
the selected tab is removed, or when an explicit `defaultValue` never
matches a mounted tab in uncontrolled roots.

For automatic changes, the selected value can be `null` when no enabled Tab
is available as a fallback.

Automatic changes cannot be canceled; calling `eventDetails.cancel()` for
`'initial'`, `'disabled'`, or `'missing'` has no effect.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the drawer is currently open.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description:
Whether the drawer is initially open.

To render a controlled drawer, use the `open` prop instead.

props.name: modal
props.description:
Determines if the drawer enters a modal state when open.
- `true`: user interaction is limited to just the drawer: focus is trapped, document page scroll is locked, and pointer interactions on outside elements are disabled.
- `false`: user interaction with the rest of the document is allowed.
- `'trap-focus'`: focus is trapped inside the drawer, but document page scroll is not locked and pointer interactions outside of it remain enabled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Event handler called when the drawer is opened or closed.

props.name: onOpenChangeComplete
props.description: Event handler called after any animations complete when the drawer is opened or closed.

props.name: disablePointerDismissal
props.description:
Whether to prevent the drawer from closing on outside presses.
For non-modal drawers, this also prevents the drawer from closing when focus moves outside of it.

props.name: actionsRef
props.description:
A ref to imperative actions: a ref object (`{ current: null }`) or a callback receiving them (and `null` on unmount).
- `unmount`: Ends the closing phase of the drawer after an externally controlled closing animation finishes.
Call `preventUnmountOnClose()` in `onOpenChange` first, otherwise the drawer completes closing on its own.
Whether it leaves the DOM is decided by `keepMounted` on the portal.
- `close`: Closes the drawer imperatively when called.

props.name: handle
props.description:
A handle to associate the drawer with a trigger.
If specified, allows detached triggers to control the drawer's open state.
Can be created with the Drawer.createHandle() method.

props.name: triggerId
props.description:
ID of the trigger that the drawer is associated with.
This is useful in conjunction with the `open` prop to create a controlled drawer.
There's no need to specify this prop when the drawer is uncontrolled (that is, when the `open` prop is not set).

props.name: defaultTriggerId
props.description:
ID of the trigger that the drawer is associated with.
This is useful in conjunction with the `defaultOpen` prop to create an initially open drawer.

props.name: swipeDirection
props.description: The swipe direction used to dismiss the drawer.

props.name: snapPoints
props.description:
Snap points used to position the drawer.
Use numbers between 0 and 1 to represent fractions of the viewport height,
numbers greater than 1 as pixel values, or strings in `px`/`rem` units
(for example, `'148px'` or `'30rem'`).

props.name: snapToSequentialPoints
props.description: Disables velocity-based snap skipping so drag distance determines the next snap point.

props.name: snapPoint
props.description: The currently active snap point. Use with `onSnapPointChange` to control the snap point.

props.name: defaultSnapPoint
props.description: The initial snap point value when uncontrolled.

props.name: onSnapPointChange
props.type: | (( snapPoint: DrawerSnapPoint | null, eventDetails: DrawerRoot.SnapPointChangeEventDetails, ) => void)
props.description: Callback fired when the snap point changes.

props.name: initialFocus
props.description:
Determines the element to focus when the drawer is opened.
By default, the popup itself is focused.

- `false`: Do not move focus.
- `true`: Move focus based on the default behavior (first tabbable element or popup).
- An element or a ref object (`{ current }`): Move focus to that element.
- `function`: Called with the interaction type (`mouse`, `touch`, `pen`, or `keyboard`).
  Return an element to focus, `true` to use the default behavior, or `false`/`undefined` to do nothing.

props.name: finalFocus
props.description:
Determines the element to focus when the drawer is closed.

- `false`: Do not move focus.
- `true`: Move focus based on the default behavior (trigger or previously focused element).
- An element or a ref object (`{ current }`): Move focus to that element.
- `function`: Called with the interaction type (`mouse`, `touch`, `pen`, or `keyboard`).
  Return an element to focus, `true` to use the default behavior, or `false`/`undefined` to do nothing.

props.description: Whether to submit the owning form when the OTP becomes complete.

props.description:

props.name: inputmode
props.description:
The virtual keyboard hint applied to the slot inputs and hidden validation input.

Built-in validation modes provide sensible defaults, but you can override them when needed.

props.name: validationType
props.description: The type of input validation to apply to the OTP value.

props.name: normalizeValue
props.description:
Function that normalizes the OTP value after whitespace and `validationType` filtering.
It runs whenever OTP Field normalizes a value, including initial/default values, controlled
values, and user edits.

The returned value is filtered by `validationType` again, then clamped to `length`.
It should be idempotent because OTP Field may normalize the same value more than once while
handling edits, storing state, and rendering controlled or uncontrolled values. Non-idempotent
normalizers can compound across those normalization passes. Characters rejected while
normalizing typed or pasted text are reported through `onValueInvalid`.

props.name: required
props.description: Whether the user must enter a value before submitting a form.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the component should ignore user interaction.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Whether the user should be unable to change the field value.

props.description: Identifies the field when a form is submitted.

props.description: The OTP value.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The uncontrolled OTP value when the component is initially rendered.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description:
Callback fired when the OTP value changes.

The `eventDetails.reason` indicates what triggered the change:
- `'input-change'` for typing or autofill
- `'input-clear'` when a character is removed by text input
- `'input-paste'` for paste interactions
- `'keyboard'` for keyboard interactions that change the value

props.name: onValueInvalid
props.description:
Callback fired when entered text contains characters that are rejected by validation or
normalization before the OTP value updates.

The `value` argument is the attempted user-entered string before normalization.

props.name: onValueComplete
props.description:
Callback function that is fired when the OTP value becomes complete, or when a complete value
is pasted while the OTP is already complete.

When the value changes, it runs later than `onValueChange`, after the internal value update is
applied. If a complete pasted value matches the current value, `onValueChange` does not fire.

If `autoSubmit` is enabled, it runs immediately before the owning form is submitted.

- `'flip'`: keep the requested side when it fits; otherwise try the opposite side
  (`top` and `bottom`, or `left` and `right`).
- `'shift'`: never change side; keep the requested side and move the popup within
  the clipping boundary so it stays visible.
- `'none'`: do not correct side-axis overflow.

`align` controls overflow on the alignment axis (`start`/`center`/`end`):
- `'flip'`: keep side, but swap `start` and `end` when the requested alignment overflows.
- `'shift'`: keep side and requested alignment, then nudge the popup along the
  alignment axis to fit.
- `'none'`: do not correct alignment-axis overflow.

preferred axis cannot fit:
- `'start'`: allow perpendicular fallback and try the logical start side first
  (`top` before `bottom`, or `left` before `right` in LTR).
- `'end'`: allow perpendicular fallback and try the logical end side first
  (`bottom` before `top`, or `right` before `left` in LTR).
- `'none'`: do not fallback to the perpendicular axis.

When `side` is `'shift'`, explicitly setting `align` only supports `'shift'` or `'none'`.
If `align` is omitted, it defaults to `'flip'`.

props.description:

props.description: Whether the highlighted item should be preserved when the pointer leaves the list.

props.description:

props.description: Event handler called after any animations complete when the popup is opened or closed.

- `list` (default): items are dynamically filtered based on the input value. The input value does not change based on the active item.

- `inline`: items are static (not filtered), and the input value will temporarily change based on the active item (inline autocompletion).
- `none`: items are static (not filtered), and the input value will not change based on the active item.

- `function`: Called with the interaction type (`mouse`, `touch`, `pen`, or `keyboard`).

props.description: Determines which CSS `position` property to use.

props.description:
Which side of the anchor element to align the popup against.

props.name: sideOffset
props.description:
Distance between the anchor and the popup in pixels.
Also accepts a function that returns the distance to read the dimensions of the anchor
and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment.

The function takes a `data` object parameter with the following properties:
- `data.anchor`: the dimensions of the anchor element with properties `width` and `height`.
- `data.positioner`: the dimensions of the positioner element with properties `width` and `height`.
- `data.side`: which side of the anchor element the positioner is aligned against.
- `data.align`: how the positioner is aligned relative to the specified side.

props.name: align
props.description: How to align the popup relative to the specified side.

props.name: alignOffset
props.description:
Additional offset along the alignment axis in pixels.
Also accepts a function that returns the offset to read the dimensions of the anchor
and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment.

The function takes a `data` object parameter with the following properties:
- `data.anchor`: the dimensions of the anchor element with properties `width` and `height`.
- `data.positioner`: the dimensions of the positioner element with properties `width` and `height`.
- `data.side`: which side of the anchor element the positioner is aligned against.
- `data.align`: how the positioner is aligned relative to the specified side.

props.description: An element or a rectangle that delimits the area that the popup is confined to.

props.name: collisionPadding
props.description: Additional space to maintain from the edge of the collision boundary.

props.name: sticky
props.description:
Whether to maintain the popup in the viewport after
the anchor element was scrolled out of view.

props.name: arrowPadding
props.description:
Minimum distance to maintain between the arrow and the edges of the popup.

Use it to prevent the arrow element from hanging out of the rounded corners of a popup.

props.name: disableAnchorTracking
props.description: Whether to disable the popup from tracking any layout shift of its positioning anchor.

props.name: collisionAvoidance
props.description:
Determines how to handle collisions when positioning the popup.

`side` controls overflow on the preferred placement axis (`top`/`bottom` or `left`/`right`):
- `'flip'`: keep the requested side when it fits; otherwise try the opposite side
  (`top` and `bottom`, or `left` and `right`).
- `'shift'`: never change side; keep the requested side and move the popup within
  the clipping boundary so it stays visible.
- `'none'`: do not correct side-axis overflow.

`align` controls overflow on the alignment axis (`start`/`center`/`end`):
- `'flip'`: keep side, but swap `start` and `end` when the requested alignment overflows.
- `'shift'`: keep side and requested alignment, then nudge the popup along the
  alignment axis to fit.
- `'none'`: do not correct alignment-axis overflow.

`fallbackAxisSide` controls fallback behavior on the perpendicular axis when the
preferred axis cannot fit:
- `'start'`: allow perpendicular fallback and try the logical start side first
  (`top` before `bottom`, or `left` before `right` in LTR).
- `'end'`: allow perpendicular fallback and try the logical end side first
  (`bottom` before `top`, or `right` before `left` in LTR).
- `'none'`: do not fallback to the perpendicular axis.

When `side` is `'shift'`, explicitly setting `align` only supports `'shift'` or `'none'`.
If `align` is omitted, it defaults to `'flip'`.

- `'start'`: allow perpendicular fallback and try the logical start side first
  (`top` before `bottom`, or `left` before `right` in LTR).
- `'end'`: allow perpendicular fallback and try the logical end side first
  (`bottom` before `top`, or `right` before `left` in LTR).
- `'none'`: do not fallback to the perpendicular axis.

When `side` is `'shift'`, explicitly setting `align` only supports `'shift'` or `'none'`.
If `align` is omitted, it defaults to `'flip'`.

props.description:
The maximum allowed value of the slider.
Should not be equal to min.

props.name: min
props.description:
The minimum allowed value of the slider.
Should not be equal to max.

props.name: minStepsBetweenValues
props.description: The minimum steps between values in a range slider.

props.name: name
props.description: Identifies the field when a form is submitted.

props.name: form
props.description:
Identifies the form that owns the slider inputs.
Useful when the slider is rendered outside the form.

props.name: orientation
props.description: The component orientation.

props.name: step
props.description:
The granularity with which the slider can step through values. (A "discrete" slider.)
The `min` prop serves as the origin for the valid values.
We recommend (max - min) to be evenly divisible by the step.

props.name: largeStep
props.description: The granularity with which the slider can step through values when using Page Up/Page Down or Shift + Arrow Up/Arrow Down.

props.name: thumbAlignment
props.description:
How the thumb(s) are aligned relative to `Slider.Control` when the value is at `min` or `max`:
- `center`: The center of the thumb is aligned with the control edge
- `edge`: The thumb is inset within the control such that its edge is aligned with the control edge
- `edge-client-only`: Same as `edge` but renders after hydration on the client, reducing bundle size in return

props.name: thumbCollisionBehavior
props.description:
Controls how thumbs behave when they collide during pointer interactions.

- `'push'` (default): Thumbs push each other without restoring their previous positions when dragged back.
- `'swap'`: Thumbs swap places when dragged past each other.
- `'none'`: Thumbs cannot move past each other; excess movement is ignored.

props.name: value
props.description:
The value of the slider.
For range sliders, provide an array with one value per thumb.

props.name: onValueChange
props.type: | (( value: Value extends number ? number : Value, eventDetails: SliderRoot.ChangeEventDetails, ) => void)
props.description:
Callback function that is fired when the slider's value changed.
Receives the new value as the first argument; the originating event is
available as `eventDetails.event`. The value is also reflected on
`eventDetails.event.target.value` for form integration.

The `eventDetails.reason` indicates what triggered the change:

- `'input-change'` when the hidden range input emits a change event (for example, via form integration)
- `'track-press'` when the control track is pressed
- `'drag'` while dragging a thumb
- `'keyboard'` for keyboard input
- `'none'` when the change is triggered without a specific interaction

props.name: onValueCommitted
props.type: | (( value: Value extends number ? number : Value, eventDetails: SliderRoot.CommitEventDetails, ) => void)
props.description:
Callback function that is fired when a value change is committed.
Does not fire if the value did not change, or if the change was canceled.
**Warning**: This is a generic event, not a change event.

The `eventDetails.reason` indicates what triggered the commit:

- `'drag'` while dragging a thumb
- `'track-press'` when the control track is pressed
- `'keyboard'` for keyboard input
- `'input-change'` when the hidden range input emits a change event (for example, via form integration)
- `'none'` when the commit occurs without a specific interaction

The function takes a `data` object parameter with the following properties:
- `data.anchor`: the dimensions of the anchor element with properties `width` and `height`.
- `data.positioner`: the dimensions of the positioner element with properties `width` and `height`.

props.description:

Also accepts a function that returns the offset to read the dimensions of the anchor
and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment.

The function takes a `data` object parameter with the following properties:
- `data.anchor`: the dimensions of the anchor element with properties `width` and `height`.
- `data.positioner`: the dimensions of the positioner element with properties `width` and `height`.

props.name: disableAnchorTracking

props.name: collisionAvoidance
props.description:
Determines how to handle collisions when positioning the popup.

`side` controls overflow on the preferred placement axis (`top`/`bottom` or `left`/`right`):
- `'flip'`: keep the requested side when it fits; otherwise try the opposite side
  (`top` and `bottom`, or `left` and `right`).
- `'shift'`: never change side; keep the requested side and move the popup within
  the clipping boundary so it stays visible.
- `'none'`: do not correct side-axis overflow.

`align` controls overflow on the alignment axis (`start`/`center`/`end`):
- `'flip'`: keep side, but swap `start` and `end` when the requested alignment overflows.
- `'shift'`: keep side and requested alignment, then nudge the popup along the
  alignment axis to fit.
- `'none'`: do not correct alignment-axis overflow.

`fallbackAxisSide` controls fallback behavior on the perpendicular axis when the
preferred axis cannot fit:
- `'start'`: allow perpendicular fallback and try the logical start side first
  (`top` before `bottom`, or `left` before `right` in LTR).
- `'end'`: allow perpendicular fallback and try the logical end side first
  (`bottom` before `top`, or `right` before `left` in LTR).
- `'none'`: do not fallback to the perpendicular axis.

When `side` is `'shift'`, explicitly setting `align` only supports `'shift'` or `'none'`.
If `align` is omitted, it defaults to `'flip'`.

and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment.

The function takes a `data` object parameter with the following properties:
- `data.anchor`: the dimensions of the anchor element with properties `width` and `height`.
- `data.positioner`: the dimensions of the positioner element with properties `width` and `height`.

props.description:

Also accepts a function that returns the offset to read the dimensions of the anchor
and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment.

The function takes a `data` object parameter with the following properties:
- `data.anchor`: the dimensions of the anchor element with properties `width` and `height`.
- `data.positioner`: the dimensions of the positioner element with properties `width` and `height`.
- `data.side`: which side of the anchor element the positioner is aligned against.

props.name: collisionAvoidance
props.description:
Determines how to handle collisions when positioning the popup.

`side` controls overflow on the preferred placement axis (`top`/`bottom` or `left`/`right`):
- `'flip'`: keep the requested side when it fits; otherwise try the opposite side
  (`top` and `bottom`, or `left` and `right`).
- `'shift'`: never change side; keep the requested side and move the popup within
  the clipping boundary so it stays visible.
- `'none'`: do not correct side-axis overflow.

`align` controls overflow on the alignment axis (`start`/`center`/`end`):
- `'flip'`: keep side, but swap `start` and `end` when the requested alignment overflows.
- `'shift'`: keep side and requested alignment, then nudge the popup along the
  alignment axis to fit.
- `'none'`: do not correct alignment-axis overflow.

`fallbackAxisSide` controls fallback behavior on the perpendicular axis when the
preferred axis cannot fit:
- `'start'`: allow perpendicular fallback and try the logical start side first
  (`top` before `bottom`, or `left` before `right` in LTR).
- `'end'`: allow perpendicular fallback and try the logical end side first

If `align` is omitted, it defaults to `'flip'`.

props.name: anchor
props.type: | Element | null | VirtualElement | RefObject<Element | null> | (() => Element | VirtualElement | null)
props.description:
An element to position the popup against.
By default, the popup will be positioned against the trigger.

Accepts an element, a virtual element, a ref object, or a function (such as a signal accessor)
that returns an element or a virtual element.

props.name: positionMethod
props.description: Determines which CSS `position` property to use.

props.name: sideOffset
props.description:
Distance between the anchor and the popup in pixels.
Also accepts a function that returns the distance to read the dimensions of the anchor
and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment.

The function takes a `data` object parameter with the following properties:
- `data.anchor`: the dimensions of the anchor element with properties `width` and `height`.
- `data.positioner`: the dimensions of the positioner element with properties `width` and `height`.
- `data.side`: which side of the anchor element the positioner is aligned against.
- `data.align`: how the positioner is aligned relative to the specified side.

props.name: alignOffset
props.description:
Additional offset along the alignment axis in pixels.
Also accepts a function that returns the offset to read the dimensions of the anchor
and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment.

The function takes a `data` object parameter with the following properties:
- `data.anchor`: the dimensions of the anchor element with properties `width` and `height`.
- `data.positioner`: the dimensions of the positioner element with properties `width` and `height`.
- `data.side`: which side of the anchor element the positioner is aligned against.
- `data.align`: how the positioner is aligned relative to the specified side.

props.name: collisionBoundary
props.description: An element or a rectangle that delimits the area that the popup is confined to.

props.name: collisionPadding
props.description: Additional space to maintain from the edge of the collision boundary.

props.name: sticky
props.description:
Whether to maintain the popup in the viewport after
the anchor element was scrolled out of view.

props.name: arrowPadding
props.description:
Minimum distance to maintain between the arrow and the edges of the popup.

Use it to prevent the arrow element from hanging out of the rounded corners of a popup.

props.name: disableAnchorTracking
props.description: Whether to disable the popup from tracking any layout shift of its positioning anchor.

props.name: collisionAvoidance
props.description:
Determines how to handle collisions when positioning the popup.

`side` controls overflow on the preferred placement axis (`top`/`bottom` or `left`/`right`):
- `'flip'`: keep the requested side when it fits; otherwise try the opposite side
  (`top` and `bottom`, or `left` and `right`).
- `'shift'`: never change side; keep the requested side and move the popup within
  the clipping boundary so it stays visible.
- `'none'`: do not correct side-axis overflow.

`align` controls overflow on the alignment axis (`start`/`center`/`end`):
- `'flip'`: keep side, but swap `start` and `end` when the requested alignment overflows.
- `'shift'`: keep side and requested alignment, then nudge the popup along the
  alignment axis to fit.
- `'none'`: do not correct alignment-axis overflow.

`fallbackAxisSide` controls fallback behavior on the perpendicular axis when the
preferred axis cannot fit:
- `'start'`: allow perpendicular fallback and try the logical start side first
  (`top` before `bottom`, or `left` before `right` in LTR).
- `'end'`: allow perpendicular fallback and try the logical end side first
  (`bottom` before `top`, or `right` before `left` in LTR).
- `'none'`: do not fallback to the perpendicular axis.

When `side` is `'shift'`, explicitly setting `align` only supports `'shift'` or `'none'`.
If `align` is omitted, it defaults to `'flip'`.

parts.name: Positioner
parts.description:
Positions the select popup.
Renders a `<div>` element.

props.name: alignItemWithTrigger
props.description: Whether the positioner overlaps the trigger so the selected item's text is aligned with the trigger's value text. This only applies to mouse input and is automatically disabled if there is not enough space.

props.name: anchor
props.type: | Element | null | VirtualElement | RefObject<Element | null> | (() => Element | VirtualElement | null)
props.description:
An element to position the popup against.
By default, the popup will be positioned against the trigger.

Accepts an element, a virtual element, a ref object, or a function (such as a signal accessor)
that returns an element or a virtual element.

props.name: positionMethod
props.description: Determines which CSS `position` property to use.

props.name: side
props.description:
Which side of the anchor element to align the popup against.
May automatically change to avoid collisions.

props.name: sideOffset
props.description:
Distance between the anchor and the popup in pixels.
Also accepts a function that returns the distance to read the dimensions of the anchor
and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment.

The function takes a `data` object parameter with the following properties:
- `data.anchor`: the dimensions of the anchor element with properties `width` and `height`.
- `data.positioner`: the dimensions of the positioner element with properties `width` and `height`.
- `data.side`: which side of the anchor element the positioner is aligned against.
- `data.align`: how the positioner is aligned relative to the specified side.

props.name: align
props.description: How to align the popup relative to the specified side.

props.name: alignOffset
props.description:
Additional offset along the alignment axis in pixels.
Also accepts a function that returns the offset to read the dimensions of the anchor
and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment.

The function takes a `data` object parameter with the following properties:
- `data.anchor`: the dimensions of the anchor element with properties `width` and `height`.
- `data.positioner`: the dimensions of the positioner element with properties `width` and `height`.
- `data.side`: which side of the anchor element the positioner is aligned against.
- `data.align`: how the positioner is aligned relative to the specified side.

props.name: collisionBoundary
props.description: An element or a rectangle that delimits the area that the popup is confined to.

props.name: collisionPadding
props.description: Additional space to maintain from the edge of the collision boundary.

props.name: sticky
props.description:
Whether to maintain the popup in the viewport after
the anchor element was scrolled out of view.

props.name: arrowPadding
props.description:
Minimum distance to maintain between the arrow and the edges of the popup.

Use it to prevent the arrow element from hanging out of the rounded corners of a popup.

props.name: disableAnchorTracking
props.description: Whether to disable the popup from tracking any layout shift of its positioning anchor.

props.name: collisionAvoidance
props.description:
Determines how to handle collisions when positioning the popup.

`side` controls overflow on the preferred placement axis (`top`/`bottom` or `left`/`right`):
- `'flip'`: keep the requested side when it fits; otherwise try the opposite side
  (`top` and `bottom`, or `left` and `right`).
- `'shift'`: never change side; keep the requested side and move the popup within
  the clipping boundary so it stays visible.
- `'none'`: do not correct side-axis overflow.

`align` controls overflow on the alignment axis (`start`/`center`/`end`):
- `'flip'`: keep side, but swap `start` and `end` when the requested alignment overflows.
- `'shift'`: keep side and requested alignment, then nudge the popup along the
  alignment axis to fit.
- `'none'`: do not correct alignment-axis overflow.

`fallbackAxisSide` controls fallback behavior on the perpendicular axis when the
preferred axis cannot fit:
- `'start'`: allow perpendicular fallback and try the logical start side first
  (`top` before `bottom`, or `left` before `right` in LTR).
- `'end'`: allow perpendicular fallback and try the logical end side first
  (`bottom` before `top`, or `right` before `left` in LTR).
- `'none'`: do not fallback to the perpendicular axis.

When `side` is `'shift'`, explicitly setting `align` only supports `'shift'` or `'none'`.
If `align` is omitted, it defaults to `'flip'`.

props.name: finalFocus
props.description:
Determines the element to focus when the select popup is closed.

- `false`: Do not move focus.
- `true`: Move focus based on the default behavior (trigger or previously focused element).
- An element or a ref object (`{ current }`): Move focus to that element.
- `function`: Called with the interaction type (`mouse`, `touch`, `pen`, or `keyboard`).
  Return an element to focus, `true` to use the default behavior, or `false`/`undefined` to do nothing.
